findings.observation: The first project-specific PHPStan rule test used PHPStan\Testing\RuleTestCase inside the normal PHPUnit process. Later WorkflowContext tests then failed inside agent-map because Composer\InstalledVersions could no longer locate phpstan/phpstan, even though the package was installed. Removing the in-process PHPStan testing runtime and executing the rule fixture in a separate PHPStan process restored the normal test matrix.

evidence.summary: CI run 31218074774 failed in four WorkflowContext tests with 'Unable to locate phpstan/phpstan installation' after the in-process RuleTestCase executed. CI run 31218247902 then passed PHP 8.3, 8.4, and 8.5 after the rule fixture moved to tools/project-phpstan-rules.sh, while the project rule itself still produced the expected diagnostic.

findings.hypothesis: Tooling test harnesses that load executable analysis runtimes into the application PHPUnit process can mutate global autoload or Composer package-discovery state and create unrelated order-dependent failures.
findings.validated_conclusion: Test agent-loop project-specific PHPStan rules in an isolated PHPStan subprocess. Do not load PHPStan\Testing\RuleTestCase into the normal agent-loop PHPUnit process while agent-map also performs Composer-based PHPStan discovery in that process.

findings.observation: The reviewed durable rule 'Tooling test isolation' states that project PHPStan rule fixtures must not load `PHPStan\Testing\RuleTestCase` into agent-loop's PHPUnit process, because agent-map performs Composer-based PHPStan discovery there. That rule was enforced only by convention: `tools/project-phpstan-rules.sh` runs the fixtures out of process, but nothing failed if somebody added an in-process `RuleTestCase` subclass beside the ordinary tests. A MEMORY row whose canonical home is a shell script is a rule with no detector.

evidence.summary: Before this change `grep -rn RuleTestCase tests/ src/ phpstan/` returned nothing, so the convention held only because no one had broken it yet. The MEMORY row named `tools/project-phpstan-rules.sh` and `phpstan/project-rule-test.neon` as its canonical home; neither can observe a new PHPUnit test class.

The isolated fixture run now reports `agentLoop.phpstan.inProcessRuleTestCase` for tests/PHPStan/data/in-process-phpstan-rule-test-case.php, and the runner asserts that exact diagnostic alongside the other eight project rules.

findings.hypothesis: Learning that stops at a MEMORY row plus a shell convention decays: the next contributor reaches for the idiomatic in-process RuleTestCase and only discovers the incompatibility as a confusing runtime failure in an unrelated suite.
findings.validated_conclusion: When a durable rule is mechanically detectable, its canonical home is the detector. This one is now `NoInProcessPhpstanRuleTestCaseRule`, and the MEMORY row points at the rule rather than at the convention that predated it.

findings.observation: A governed Recall compilation selected approved proposal.2026-08-14.004 and blocked because its validation references tools/project-phpstan-rules.sh, which no longer exists; the live deterministic runner is tools/project-phpstan-rules.php.

evidence.summary: Recall blocked selected guidance proposal.2026-08-14.004 because validation names missing tools/project-phpstan-rules.sh.
The approved validation command names tools/project-phpstan-rules.sh while the current executable is tools/project-phpstan-rules.php.

findings.hypothesis: An approved guidance record and its detector drifted during the shell-to-PHP runner migration, so Recall preserves the stale path as a fail-closed blocker instead of emitting unusable guidance.
findings.validated_conclusion: Correct a durable guidance entry toward the live executable command and bind the already-existing detector as an adopted static constraint; do not add another prose rule or duplicate analyzer.
